Recall that displacement is the signed area under a $v$-$t$ graph, so area below the time axis counts as negative.
Calculate the two signed areas separately, add them for net displacement, then divide by the total time of $15 \text{ s}$.
walkthrough: Identify the motion from the $v$-$t$ graph: constant $+3.0 \text{ m s}^{-1}$ for $10 \text{ s}$, then constant $-6.0 \text{ m s}^{-1}$ for $5 \text{ s}$.
Use the rule that displacement equals signed area under $v$-$t$: $\text{displacement} = v \times t$ for each rectangle, keeping the sign of $v$.
Forward displacement is $+3.0 \times 10 = +30 \text{ m}$ and reverse displacement is $-6.0 \times 5 = -30 \text{ m}$.
Add for net displacement: $+30 + (-30) = 0 \text{ m}$, so the car returns to its start.
Average velocity is net displacement divided by total time: $0/15 = 0.0 \text{ m s}^{-1}$. This is option B.
